message:
Before VLANs, a check on how a switch learns.

```quiz
{"mode":"practice","questions":[{"type":"short","question":"Why does a switch flood a unicast frame out of every port except the one it arrived on?","keyPoints":[["unknown unicast","not in the MAC address table","not in its MAC address table","not in the MAC table"],["learn","learns","learning"]],"sample":"The destination MAC address is not in its MAC address table yet (unknown unicast), so it floods the frame and learns where the host is from the reply.","explanation":"A switch forwards on what it has learned; until the destination answers, flooding is the only way to reach it."},{"question":"Which protocol resolves an IPv4 address to a MAC address on the local segment?","options":["ARP","DNS","DHCP","ICMP"],"answer":"A","explanation":"ARP maps a next-hop IPv4 address to the hardware address that frames are sent to."}]}
```
